articles.content: LONDON (Reuters) -Countries that see themselves as U.S. allies are now considering whether President Donald Trump's administration could one day disrupt their payments systems to exert diplomatic pressure, a former top Bank of England official has said. Jon Cunliffe, the BoE's deputy governor for financial stability from 2014 to 2024, said Western countries relied heavily on U.S.-headquartered Visa and Mastercard for day-to-day domestic transactions and found it hard to avoid U.S. banks when making foreign payments.
